mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact corporate earnings and drive up stock prices, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 20-day periods, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate suggests easier monetary policy, which can stimulate investment and consumption, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by 0.5% in the last month
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the triggered instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and higher corporate revenues, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by 0.2 percentage points in the last month
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
